outcomes.question: What are the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
outcomes.answer: The six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 13]
outcomes.modelOutput: {"status":"ANSWERED","claims":[{"text":"The six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability.","ref":"r1c2","quote":"When architecting technology solutions, if you neglect the six pillars of operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability, it can become challenging to build a system that delivers on your expectations and requirements."}]}

outcomes.question: Why does the framework advise to stop guessing capacity needs?
outcomes.answer:
Making a poor capacity decision can result in paying for expensive idle resources or facing the performance impacts of limited capacity. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 11]
In cloud computing, these capacity problems are eliminated because you can use whatever capacity is required and scale automatically. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 11]
Workloads in on-premises environments frequently fail due to resource saturation when workload demands surpass capacity. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]

You can use as much or as little capacity as you need, and scale in and out automatically."},{"text":"Workloads in on-premises environments frequently fail due to resource saturation when workload demands surpass capacity.","ref":"r1c3","quote":"A common cause of failure in on-premises workloads is resource saturation, when the demands placed on a workload exceed the capacity of that workload"}]}

outcomes.question: What is the difference between one-way door and two-way door decisions?
outcomes.answer:
Two-way door decisions are reversible and can utilize a lightweight process. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 69]
One-way doors are difficult or impossible to reverse, requiring greater inspection prior to being made. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 69]

outcomes.question: What is the AWS Well-Architected Tool?
outcomes.answer:
The AWS Well-Architected Tool is a service in the cloud that provides a consistent process for reviewing and measuring architecture using the AWS Well-Architected Framework. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The AWS Well-Architected Tool offers recommendations to make workloads more reliable, secure, efficient, and cost-effective. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
AWS provides the service for reviewing workloads at no charge. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The AWS Well-Architected Tool helps review your approach prior to development, workload state prior to production, and workload state in production. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 12]

outcomes.question: What does recovery time objective (RTO) mean?
outcomes.answer:
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) refers to the maximum acceptable delay between service interruption and service restoration. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 680]
RTO establishes an acceptable time window during which a service can be unavailable, as determined by the organization. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 13]
Unlike Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR), which represents a mean value across several events, RTO is a target or maximum allowed value for a single availability-impacting event. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 19]

outcomes.question: How should a client retry failed requests without overloading a service?
outcomes.answer:
Adding exponential backoff with jitter to client retries permits servers to recover from failures caused by resource overload. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Jitter prevents requests from aligning into traffic spikes, while backoff lessens load escalation caused by combining retries with regular traffic. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
A maximum number of retries or elapsed time should be configured to prevent backlogs that lead to metastable failures. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Exponential backoff retries requests after progressively longer intervals, while jitter randomizes the intervals. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Retries should be implemented at only one level of the application stack to avoid compounding attempts into a retry storm. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]

outcomes.question: Why should a workload be aware of service quotas and constraints?
outcomes.answer:
Being aware of and managing service quotas and constraints helps customers prevent service degradation or disruption in their AWS accounts. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 470]
Monitoring and automatically managing service quotas and resource constraints can proactively minimize failures. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 470]
If a constraint is reached unexpectedly, an account's services or applications might suffer degradation or disruption. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 24]

outcomes.question: How does the reliability pillar suggest recovering automatically from failures?
outcomes.answer:
Automation can be triggered when a threshold is breached by monitoring a workload for key performance indicators (KPIs). [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]
Key performance indicators should measure business value rather than the technical operation aspects of the service. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]
Monitoring KPIs provides automatic notification and tracking of failures, as well as automated recovery processes that work around or repair the failure. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]
More sophisticated automation makes it possible to anticipate and remediate failures before they occur. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]

outcomes.question: Who is responsible for what in the shared responsibility model for security?
outcomes.answer:
Under Security of the Cloud, AWS is responsible for protecting the infrastructure that runs all of the services offered in the AWS Cloud, which includes hardware, software, networking, and facilities. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
AWS operates, manages, and controls components from the host operating system and virtualization layer down to the physical security of facilities. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Customer responsibility, or Security in the Cloud, is determined by the specific AWS Cloud services chosen by the customer. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Customers assume responsibility for managing the guest operating system, including updates and security patches, associated application software, and configuration of the AWS-provided security group firewall. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]

This infrastructure is composed of the hardware, software, networking, and facilities that run AWS Cloud services."},{"text":"AWS operates, manages, and controls components from the host operating system and virtualization layer down to the physical security of facilities.","ref":"r1c1","quote":"AWS operates, manages, and controls the components from the host operating system and virtualization layer down to the physical security of the facilities in which the service operates."},{"text":"Customer responsibility, or Security in the Cloud, is determined by the specific AWS Cloud services chosen by the customer.","ref":"r1c1","quote":"Customer responsibility “Security in the Cloud” – Customer responsibility will be determined by the AWS Cloud services that a customer selects."},{"text":"Customers assume responsibility for managing the guest operating system, including updates and security patches, associated application software, and configuration of the AWS-provided security group firewall.","ref":"r1c1","quote":"The customer assumes responsibility and management of the guest operating system (including updates and security patches), and other associated application software in addition to the configuration of the AWS provided security group firewall."}]}

outcomes.question: How should secrets and credentials be managed and rotated?
outcomes.answer:
The best approach to secrets management is to follow the principles of remove, replace, and rotate. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 49]
Whenever possible, long-term credentials should be replaced with temporary or short-term credentials, such as using IAM roles. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 49]
Long-lived secrets that cannot be removed or replaced can be centrally stored, managed, and regularly rotated using a service such as AWS Secrets Manager. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 300]
Application and database credentials should be stored in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation established if possible. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 301]
OAuth tokens, API tokens, and keys can also be stored in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation configured. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 301]
When communication with AWS services requires access keys, temporary security credentials should be used instead of embedding keys in code or apps. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 301]

outcomes.question: What is the principle of least privilege?
outcomes.answer:
The principle of least privilege states that identities should only be allowed to perform the smallest set of actions required to carry out a specific task. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]
This principle balances usability, efficiency, and security. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]
Operating under the principle of least privilege helps limit unintended access and assists in tracking who has access to specific resources. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]

outcomes.question: How does the operational excellence pillar recommend making changes to workloads?
outcomes.answer:
The operational excellence pillar recommends making frequent, small, and reversible changes to workloads. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Using automated deployment techniques alongside smaller, incremental changes lowers the blast radius and allows for quicker reversal when failures happen. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Frequent, small, and reversible changes reduce the scope and impact of changes, leading to more effective troubleshooting and faster remediation with rollback capabilities. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 119]

outcomes.question: What are runbooks used for?
outcomes.answer:
A runbook is a documented process used to achieve a specific outcome. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
In cloud operations, runbooks are utilized to reduce risk and accomplish desired outcomes. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
Runbooks often serve routine activities and achieve specific outcomes, in contrast to playbooks that respond to non-routine events. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]
Runbooks remain useful for conducting game days and satisfying reporting and auditing requirements. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]

outcomes.answer:
Feature flags and A/B testing can be used to safely experiment and gather user feedback. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 128]

AWS Lambda versions can be used to deploy a new function version for beta testing. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 128]

outcomes.question: What does democratize advanced technologies mean in the performance efficiency pillar?
outcomes.answer:
Democratizing advanced technologies means making advanced technology implementation easier for your team by delegating complex tasks to your cloud vendor. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Instead of asking an IT team to learn about hosting and running a new technology, organizations should consider consuming the technology as a service. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Technologies requiring specialized expertise include NoSQL databases, media transcoding, and machine learning. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
In the cloud, these technologies become consumable services, enabling teams to focus on product development instead of resource provisioning and management. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]

outcomes.answer:
Mechanical sympathy involves understanding how cloud services are consumed and always choosing the technology approach that aligns with your workload goals. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 45]

outcomes.question: How should failed Lambda transactions be retained and retried?
outcomes.answer:
A dead-letter queue mechanism should be used to retain, investigate, and retry failed transactions. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Failed transactions in AWS Lambda can be directed to a dedicated Amazon SQS dead-letter queue on a per function basis. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
To control retry and remove poison-pill messages, AWS Lambda lets you configure Maximum Retry Attempts, Maximum Record Age, and Destination on Failure. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]

outcomes.question: What options does AWS offer for service discovery of microservices?
outcomes.answer:
Amazon ECS provides integrated service discovery allowing containerized services to discover and connect with each other. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 16]
Amazon ECS creates and manages a registry of service names utilizing the Route 53 Auto Naming API. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Unified service discovery can be used for services managed by Kubernetes, supported by AWS's contribution to the External DNS project. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
AWS Cloud Map provides an API-based service discovery mechanism and extends the capabilities of the Auto Naming APIs. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Third-party software such as HashiCorp Consul, etcd, or Netflix Eureka can also be used to implement service discovery. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Service meshes represent an additional layer for handling interservice communication that can completely handle tasks like service discovery. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]

outcomes.question: What do twelve-factor processes say about state?
outcomes.answer:
Twelve-factor processes are stateless and share-nothing. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 14]
Any data needing to persist must be kept in a stateful backing service, typically a database. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 14]

outcomes.question: What does it mean to adopt a consumption model?
outcomes.answer: Adopting a consumption model means paying only for the computing resources consumed, while increasing or decreasing usage based on business requirements. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 8]

outcomes.question: How does the cost optimization pillar suggest reducing cloud waste?
outcomes.answer:
Organizations should identify and recoup spend associated with cloud waste for deployed resources. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Cloud waste happens when resources of incorrect size are created or when unexpected usage patterns are observed. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Organizations are advised to follow AWS best practices or seek assistance from their account team and partner to reduce waste and optimize cloud costs. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Attributing resource costs to workloads, individual organizations, or product owners promotes efficient usage behavior and aids in reducing waste. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 37]

outcomes.question: Why does the choice of AWS Region matter for the carbon footprint of a workload?
outcomes.answer:
The choice of Region for a workload significantly affects KPIs including performance, cost, and carbon footprint. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 62]
Placing a workload near Amazon renewable energy projects or in Regions with low published carbon intensity can help reduce its cloud carbon footprint. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 935]

outcomes.question: What is the shared responsibility model for sustainability?
outcomes.answer:
Environmental sustainability is a shared responsibility between customers and AWS. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]
AWS is responsible for the sustainability of the cloud, which involves delivering efficient, shared infrastructure, water stewardship, and sourcing renewable power. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]
Customers bear responsibility for sustainability in the cloud by optimizing workloads and resource utilization, as well as minimizing total deployed resources. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]

outcomes.question: What does AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery do?
outcomes.answer:
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates server-hosted applications and server-hosted databases from any source into AWS via block-level replication of the underlying server. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
It allows a Region in the AWS Cloud to serve as a disaster recovery target for workloads hosted on-premises or on another cloud provider. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
For AWS-hosted workloads, it can be utilized for disaster recovery if they comprise exclusively applications and databases hosted on EC2 rather than RDS. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
When using Elastic Disaster Recovery, the service coordinates and orchestrates compute resource recovery upon initiation during a drill or failover. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 692]
When a failover event is triggered, staged resources are used to automatically establish a full-capacity deployment in the target Amazon VPC recovery location. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 27]
